title: Crosswalk for company priority maps and tactical slices
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Purpose:
Create a reusable crosswalk artifact that maps company-level OKRs and strategic pillars to deliverable-level initiatives (quarterly tactical slices). This crosswalk will be the single source for prioritization conversations during planning and for automated visibility in the Console roadmap dashboards.

Goals:
- Make the mapping from company objectives to tactical work explicit and discoverable for all stakeholders.
- Provide capacity guidance (bandwidth slices) per initiative so PMs and Eng leads can quantify trade-offs during committed planning.
- Introduce a lightweight escalation path and decision radar for conflicts when capacity or dependencies block an initiative.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
1) A documented Crosswalk Canvas template that teams use to map 1 company objective -> 2-4 initiatives -> 3-6 sprint-level tactical slices. (Template published to Confluence)
2) A populated company-level Crosswalk for Q1 2026 with owners, estimates, and top-3 risks for each initiative.
3) A small integration with the roadmap dashboard that surfaces top-level mapping and capacity signals (PRD + demo).
4) A playbook for resolving priority conflicts (timelines, escalation roles, decision timeboxes) and measurement rubric for OKR-health signals.

Scope notes (in-scope):
- Design template, Confluence host page, and a CSV import/export format for the roadmap tool.
- One-off population of the Crosswalk for company OKRs for Q1 2026.
- Lightweight integration to surface mapping in Console roadmap view (data polymap + link outs).

Out of scope:
- Full automation with ticket-level syncing (future follow-up).
- Enforcement or gating of engineering sprints via the Crosswalk (we'll provide guidance, not a blocker).

Stakeholders & roles:
- PM lead: Priya Nair (owner)
- Eng lead: Miguel Santos (technical feasibility & dependency owner)
- Design: Lena Cho (template & UX for Canvas)
- GTM: Sasha Kim (go-to-market signals & customer-facing language)
- Analytics: Jordan Patel (metrics & dashboarding)
- Ops: Claire Reynolds (escalation and capacity policy)

Success metrics (how we will measure success):
- 90% of cross-functional leads confirm the mapping as accurate during planning readout (survey).
- Roadmap dashboard shows crosswalk linkage for >= 85% of company-level initiatives.
- Time-to-decision for conflicting priorities reduced from median 6 days to <= 48 hours during the planning window.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (Nov 18–24): Draft Canvas + review with Design and Eng leads.
- Week 2 (Nov 25–Dec 1): Populate Q1 company crosswalk with initiative owners; review with exec sponsor.
- Week 3 (Dec 2–8): Build CSV import and small Console surface prototype; open experimental access to PMs.
- Week 4 (Dec 9–15): Run planning readout, collect feedback, publish playbook and Confluence page.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Teams will not keep the Crosswalk updated. Mitigation: include lightweight CSV export/import and one-click links to initiative owner’s Linear tickets; schedule a monthly 15-minute sync.
- Risk: Capacity estimates will be inconsistent. Mitigation: provide a standard estimate scale (T-shirt sizes mapped to points) and a short estimation guide in the template.
- Risk: Execs escalate tactical decisions too often. Mitigation: define clear escalation thresholds and timeboxes in the playbook.
